brief:
Our county library board meets Thursday and wants to change how overdue fines work. There are three ideas floating around and I can't tell which is best from a wall of text. Can you build me a page where I can explore different ways this could be implemented and compare them? Last year's numbers from the circulation report are below, then the three proposals.

Branch | Items Out (count) | Overdue Rate (%) | Fines Billed ($) | Fines Collected ($) | Cardholders Blocked | Notes
Main Street | 48,212 | 6.4% | $31,480.50 | $12,905.25 | 1,204 | Biggest block count; "temporary" desk staffed 2 days/wk
O'Brien Memorial | 9,870 | 8.1% | $7,102.00 | $2,311.75 | 388 |
St. Anne's (Eastside) | 12,455 | 9.9% | $10,964.80 | $3,090.00 | 502 | Lots of kids' cards; parents dispute charges
Riverbend | 6,018 | 4.2% | $1,845.25 | $1,402.10 | 61 |
Hollis; Annex | 3,340 | 11.3% | $3,771.00 | $604.50 | 219 | Bookmobile stop; "no fines" signs up since March
Quarry Hill | 7,902 | 7.0% | $4,230.60 | $1,988.00 | 247 |
Dunmore | 5,115 | 5.5% | $2,260.00 | $1,512.40 | 90 | Pays by check only
Lakeside (seasonal) | 2,640 | | $980.00 | $415.00 | 33 | Open May-Sept only
Harlan Road | 8,731 | 7.7% | $5,674.35 | $2,105.90 | 301 |
Veterans' Branch, North | 11,206 | 8.8% | $8,803.20 | $3,447.65 | 436 | Lost-item fees mixed in; can't separate them
Mill Creek | 4,477 | 3.9% | $1,320.00 | $1,198.00 | 40 |
Tannery Row | 6,903 | 10.2% | $6,218.50 | $1,022.00 | 355 | Teens, after-school crowd

Proposal A: End daily fines entirely; charge a flat $5.00 replacement fee once an item is 30 days late.
Proposal B: Cap fines at $10.00 per item, and one-time "forgive and reset" for any account under $25.
Proposal C: Fine-free for cards under 18 only; adults unchanged, but the blocking threshold rises from $10 to $25.

What I need to tell the board is what each one does to revenue and to the number of blocked cardholders, branch by branch where it matters. I don't trust my own guesses about how people would behave, so I'd like to be able to change the assumptions myself and see what happens. Flag anywhere the data above is too thin to support a conclusion.

I run harvest logistics for a small estate winery and I need to decide between three ways of getting the fruit in this year. I keep redrawing these in my notebook and losing track. Please make me a page that lays out the options so I can compare the plans against each other and see where each one breaks.

Block | Variety | Area (ha) | Brix (deg) | Est. Yield (t) | Pick Window | Contract ($/t) | Notes
N1 | Pinot Noir | 2.4 | 23.1 | 11.5 | Sep 14-18 | $2,850 | Sparkling base; must be hand-picked
N2 | Pinot Noir | 1.8 | 22.4 | 8.2 | Sep 16-21 | $2,850 | Mildew pressure on east rows
S3 | Chardonnay | 3.1 | 21.8 | 19.0 | Sep 12-17 | $2,100 |
S4 | Chardonnay | 2.2 | 22.9 | 13.4 | Sep 15-20 | $2,100 | Machine OK
E5 | Syrah | 4.0 | 24.6 | 22.8 | Sep 28-Oct 6 | $1,975 | "Dad's block": oldest vines, planted 1987
E6 | Syrah | 1.6 | | 7.9 | Sep 30-Oct 7 | $1,975 | Sunburn on west face; needs sorting table
W7 | Riesling | 2.7 | 20.3 | 14.6 | Sep 20-27 | $1,640 | Late-harvest option (ask Priya)
W8 | Riesling | 1.1 | 20.9 | 5.2 | Sep 21-28 | $1,640 |
M9 | Merlot | 3.3 | 23.7 | 18.1 | Oct 2-10 | $1,880 | Birds; netting torn in 3 rows
M10 | Cabernet Franc | 1.9 | 24.0 | 9.3 | Oct 4-12 | $2,320 | Reserve label (single-vineyard)

Resources: two hand crews of 14 people each; one person picks about 1.2 t per day by hand. The machine harvester is rented for Sep 15-22 only, at $1,350 per day, and it can't touch N1, N2 or E5. A third hand crew costs $4,100 per week if I can get one. Sorting table runs at 6 t per day.

Plans I'm weighing:
1. Hand-pick everything and hire the third crew for three weeks.
2. Machine for the Chardonnay and Riesling that fit its dates; hand crews for the rest.
3. Hold the Riesling for late harvest and push all the labor into the reds.

I want to see each plan's labor days, rental cost, which blocks get picked outside their window, and what the Riesling gamble could cost or earn. Tell me where the numbers above leave something undecidable.

Background from the ticket: customers on the Harbourline account were over-billed a total of $1,482.37 across 6,213 invoices between Aug 1 and Oct 9, because the surcharge of 7.35% was rounded after summing lines instead of per line. Average error was about $0.24 per invoice, max $3.10. Credits for the over-billing are a separate ticket (FIN-2210) and are not part of this change. Invoices finalized before Oct 1 are not recalculated.

Please write the description so a reviewer knows the problem, what changed, how it was checked, what could still go wrong, and what to look at first. Be honest about the 28 replay differences and the two skipped tests.

I've been asked to review a pull request on our air-quality sensor firmware and I'm out of my depth with the interrupt code. The branch is checked out. Please review it for me and give me something I can work through before I approve or push back. Here's the change summary and the discussion so far.

Title: "Sleep between samples: cut idle draw, fix PM2.5 drift (#318)"
Author: Marguerite Oyelaran

File | Lines Added | Lines Removed | Reviewer Comments
src/power/sleep.c | 142 | 38 | 3
src/sensors/pm25.c | 57 | 61 | 2
src/sensors/pm25_calib.h | 9 | 3 | 0
src/net/uplink.c | 24 | 5 | 1
boards/rev_d/pins.h | 6 | 6 | 0
test/sim/sleep_wake_test.c | 188 | 0 | 0
CHANGELOG | 7 | 0 | 0

Comments so far:
Tobias Lindqvist on sleep.c: "Why is the wake interrupt re-armed before the fan spin-up delay? Looks racy."
Marguerite on sleep.c: "It's armed early on purpose so we don't miss the 'rain event' pin, but I'll add a comment."
Tobias on sleep.c: "Deep sleep current measured at 11 uA (was 46 uA). What's the battery life claim based on? 2,400 mAh / 11 uA is way more than 3 years once the radio is counted."
Priya Nair on pm25.c: "The drift fix changes the baseline from 5-min to 30-min rolling; that will hide real spikes (wildfire smoke, e.g.)."
Priya on pm25.c: "Also unit test missing for sensor timeout (> 2.5 s)?"
Ben O'Callaghan on uplink.c: "Retry count dropped from 5 to 3; was that intentional? Field units at Ridgeway had 18% packet loss in July."

PR description claims: 76% less idle power, "no change to reporting interval", battery life "3+ years" (previously about 14 months).

CI: 58 of 58 simulated tests pass; hardware-in-loop job (bench rig 2) has not run since Oct 9.

Tell me what is actually risky, which review comments are still unanswered or answered weakly, and which claims in the description I should ask the author to back up.

I just joined the platform team of a ferry-booking company and everyone keeps saying "retries pile up when the vessel-status service gets slow" but nobody can explain exactly how. The repo is checked out. I'd like to actually understand how retries and timeouts are configured across the services, how they compound along a booking request, and where the worst-case wait really comes from. Below is a settings dump someone pulled from production last week; please check it against what the code really does, since I suspect it's out of date.

Service | Max Attempts | Initial Delay (ms) | Multiplier | Max Delay (s) | Timeout per Try (s) | Jitter (%) | Notes
booking-api | 3 | 200 | 2.0 | 5 | 10 | 20 | Entry point; calls the next three
fare-calculator | 4 | 100 | 1.5 | 2 | 3 | 10 |
vessel-status | 5 | 250 | 2.0 | 8 | 4 | 0 | "Temporary" no-jitter since the March outage
seat-inventory | 3 | 150 | 2.0 | 3 | 5 | 25 | Calls vessel-status for capacity
payment-gateway | 2 | 500 | 3.0 | 10 | 15 | 15 | Third-party; their SLA is 99.5%
notification-svc | 6 | 1,000 | 2.0 | 60 | 5 | 30 | Async; shouldn't block bookings
port-schedule-sync | 8 | 2,000 | 1.5 | 120 | 20 | | Nightly job
loyalty-points | 3 | 300 | 2.0 | 4 | 6 | 20 | Failures are swallowed; see ticket OPS-5521
refund-worker | 5 | 750 | 2.5 | 30 | 12 | 10 | Dead-letter after last attempt

Extra context: during the incident on Sept 3 the booking error rate hit 38% for 41 minutes and p99 latency was 74 s against a normal 1.9 s. The load balancer in front of booking-api times out at 30 s.

Please walk me through it so I come away understanding the mechanism, not just the numbers: who calls whom, what the real worst case is for one customer clicking "Book now", where retries multiply, and which settings look like mistakes or leftovers. Where the dump and the code disagree, say so and tell me which to trust.

I'm the designer for a science museum's wayfinding and signage program, and our design tokens live in a messy shared document that nobody reads. I'd like a proper reference artifact for the system, something new hires and the sign vendor could both open and understand without asking me questions. Here's what's in the document today; it's incomplete and some entries contradict each other.

Token | Value | Used For | Notes
color.ink | #1B1F23 | Body text on light signs |
color.paper | #F7F3EA | Sign backgrounds (warm white) | Vendor calls this "Bone 04"
color.wayfind-blue | #0B5FA5 | Primary route markers | Fails contrast on color.paper at small sizes?
color.hazard | #D93A00 | Exits, warnings | Never use for decoration
color.gallery-green | #2E7D4F | Natural history wing |
color.gallery-violet | #6A3FA0 | Space and physics wing |
color.gallery-ochre | #C98A16 | Ancient worlds wing | Text on ochre must be ink, not paper
color.accessible-focus | | Tactile and large-print signs | TBD with the accessibility consultant
type.display | "Alder Grotesk" Bold, 120 mm cap height | Gallery entrance signs | Max 22 characters
type.wayfind | "Alder Grotesk" Medium, 60 mm | Directional signs |
type.label | "Alder Grotesk" Regular, 24 mm | Exhibit labels | Viewing distance 1.2 m

space.margin-sign | 40 mm | Inside edge of any sign |
space.icon-gap | 18 mm | Between icon and text |

Build me a reference page for this system. Show the tokens in a way that makes the relationships obvious, show examples of how they combine on realistic signs, and point out the gaps and contradictions you find (the blue on paper contrast, the blank focus color, the vendor's different name for the paper color). Don't invent values I haven't given; mark proposed values as proposals.

We're updating the departures board that runs in the concourse of a regional rail station, and I want to prototype how the rows animate when a train's status changes. Right now rows just flip instantly and passengers miss changes. I can't describe the motion I want, so I need to see it and adjust it by feel. Here's the component inventory and the current timings from our spec sheet.

Component | Size (px) | Current Motion | Duration (ms) | Notes
Row container | 1920 x 96 | none | 0 | 14 rows visible, scrolls when more
Platform badge | 72 x 72 | instant swap | 0 | Needs to draw the eye; "Platform 4" changes most
Destination text | 640 x 56 | instant swap | 0 | Names such as St. Pancras Int'l, Llanfairpwllgwyngyll (long!)
Scheduled time | 160 x 56 | none | 0 | 24-hour, monospaced digits
Expected time | 160 x 56 | fade | 150 | Turns amber when delayed
Status pill | 220 x 48 | instant swap | 0 | On time / Delayed / Cancelled / Boarding
Delay minutes | 120 x 48 | none | | Shows "+12 min"
Boarding indicator | 24 x 24 | blink | 1,000 | Green dot; 1 Hz per accessibility review
Cancelled strike-through | 1,100 x 4 | none | 0 | Draws across the row
Row reorder (new departure inserted) | 1920 x 96 | jump | 0 | Rows below shift down 96 px
Alert banner | 1920 x 140 | slide from top | 300 | Used for platform changes and evacuations

Some facts: the board is read from 5 to 30 meters away; a quarter of our passengers are over 65; the commuter rush has about 6 status changes per minute at peak; the cancelled-train case has to be unmistakable but not alarming; and the screens run on cheap hardware that drops frames if more than 3 rows animate at once. Accessibility wants a reduced-motion version that never moves anything, only changes color or opacity. Our brand colors are deep teal #0E4D5C, signal amber #F2A900, and signal red #C8102E.

Please make me something where I can see these components move and try different timings, easing curves and orders of events for each change type (delay, platform change, cancellation, new departure inserted), then settle on values I can hand to the developers. Start with what you'd recommend and explain why, but let me override.

We had an incident at our cold-chain warehouse last Thursday and I need to write it up for the client and for our insurer. I have the event log and a few notes, but I'm not a writer. Please produce the incident report as a page I can send. The audience is a pharmacy distributor's quality manager (they care about product temperature and whether any of their stock needs to be quarantined) and our own operations director.

Time (local) | Source | Event | Temp (C) | Notes
02:14 | Freezer 3 sensor | Door open alarm | -21.4 | Night shift loading dock B
02:19 | Freezer 3 sensor | Door open alarm cleared | -19.8 |
03:40 | Compressor B | Fault code E-41 (low suction pressure) | -20.1 | Auto-switched to Compressor A
03:41 | Compressor A | Overload trip | -20.0 | Not logged by BMS until 03:58
03:58 | BMS | "Compressor offline" warning sent | -19.2 | Sent to on-call phone of Kwame Asante
04:05 | Freezer 3 sensor | Temp above -18 limit | -17.6 | Alarm threshold is -18.0 per SOP
04:20 | Kwame Asante | Phone silent; no ack | | Phone was on charge in another room, he says
04:35 | BMS | Escalation to backup (Lucia Ferreira) | -15.1 |
04:52 | Lucia Ferreira | Acked; arrives on site | -12.9 | 17 min drive
05:10 | Facilities | Manual reset of Compressor A | -11.2 | Reset worked; compressor running
05:55 | Freezer 3 sensor | Temp trending down | -14.6 |
07:30 | Freezer 3 sensor | Back below -18 | -18.3 | 3 h 25 min total above limit
07:45 | QA (Mei-Lin Zhao) | Quarantine tag applied to pallets 3-14 to 3-31 | | 18 pallets, ~$286,400 stock at invoice value
09:00 | QA | Probe readings of product core taken | -17.1 | Core temps are what matter; peak core not recorded

Extra facts: product in freezer 3 belongs to three clients; the distributor's stock is the 18 pallets. Their stability data allows excursions up to -10 C for a maximum of 4 hours cumulative, but the peak air temperature was -11.2 C and nobody measured how warm the cores got. Compressor B's service was last done 14 months ago against a 12-month schedule. A third alarm channel (SMS to the shift supervisor) was proposed in April and never done. Total estimated cost so far: $9,850 for the call-out, repairs, and extra QA time.

Write it plainly. I want the timeline, impact, what we know versus what we don't, root causes, and corrective actions with owners and dates (propose dates; I'll confirm). Don't hide that the alarm response was slow.

I'm the operations analyst at a mid-sized property insurer and I've been asked to explain to our new VP, who's never worked in claims, how a homeowner's water-damage claim actually moves through the company and why it takes so long. She wants to understand the flow, see where claims wait, and see where we lose money on rework. Please build a page for her. The numbers below are from the claims operations dashboard for Q3.

Step | Team | Median Time (days) | 90th pct (days) | Claims Entering (count) | Sent Back (%) | Notes
First notice of loss | Contact center | 0.1 | 0.4 | 4,812 | 3.1% | Phone 61%, app 33%, agent 6%
Coverage check | Policy services | 0.9 | 3.2 | 4,812 | 6.8% | Lapsed or "non-owner occupied" policies get stuck here
Assign adjuster | Dispatch | 1.4 | 6.0 | 4,483 | 1.2% | Backlog after the Sept 11 storm
Field inspection | Field adjusters | 3.8 | 11.5 | 4,429 | 9.4% | Needs homeowner's availability; reschedules count
Estimate & scope | Desk adjusters | 2.2 | 7.1 | 4,012 | 14.7% | Biggest rework; contractor estimates disagree
Supervisor approval (> $10,000) | Claims supervisors | 1.9 | 9.8 | 1,206 | 5.5% | Under $10,000 skips this step
Fraud screen | Special investigations | 0.6 | 2.0 | 4,012 | 2.3% | 187 referred for full review (3.9%)
Payment issued | Finance | 1.1 | 2.7 | 3,794 | 0.8% | Checks vs. direct deposit: 44% / 56%
Mitigation vendor dispatch | Vendor mgmt | 0.7 | 1.9 | 2,950 | | Runs in parallel with inspection for urgent cases
Closure & survey | Claims admin | 4.0 | 14.0 | 3,794 | 0% | Survey response rate 17%

Other numbers: average claim paid is $14,238.60 (median $7,905); the cost of one rework loop is about $212 in staff time; 22% of claims are reopened within 90 days; customer satisfaction is 71 for claims that take under 14 days and 38 for those over 30.

Show her the path a claim takes, including the branches (supervisor approval, fraud referral, mitigation vendor, send-backs), where time is spent and where claims pile up, and what the rework costs in total. Make clear which numbers are medians and which are the slow tail; she'll otherwise add the median column up and assume that's the whole wait. Explain insurance terms the first time they appear, and keep the focus on what she can do something about.

I manage irrigation for a 40-acre orchard and the controller's schedule is a long list of numbers I edit by hand and regularly get wrong. Last month I accidentally ran two big zones at once and tripped the pump. I want a proper way to edit this schedule where it stops me from breaking the rules, and where I can pick the start times and days without doing math in my head. Here's the current schedule exported from the controller.

Zone | Crop | Start Time | Run Time (min) | Days | Flow (L/min) | Soil Moisture (%) | Notes
Z1 | Honeycrisp apples | 05:00 | 75 | Mon, Thu | 310 | 24.5 | Young trees, planted 2023
Z2 | Honeycrisp apples | 06:30 | 75 | Mon, Thu | 310 | 26.1 |
Z3 | Fuji apples | 05:30 | 60 | Tue, Fri | 280 | 21.8 | Drains fast; sandy patch near the road
Z4 | Fuji apples | 07:00 | 60 | Tue, Fri | 280 | 27.3 |
Z5 | Bartlett pears | 04:30 | 90 | Wed, Sat | 345 | 30.2 | "Wet corner" in NE rows; check for leaks
Z6 | Bartlett pears | 06:15 | 90 | Wed, Sat | 345 | 29.7 |
Z7 | Cherries (Bing) | 05:45 | 45 | Mon, Wed, Fri | 220 | 19.4 | Needs deficit stress before harvest; do not exceed 45 min
Z8 | Cherries (Rainier) | 06:30 | 45 | Mon, Wed, Fri | 220 | | Sensor broken since Sept
Z9 | Nursery rows | 19:00 | 30 | Daily | 95 | 33.8 | Hand-watered Sundays
Z10 | Plum (Santa Rosa) | 21:30 | 80 | Tue, Sat | 260 | 25.0 |

Rules I live with: the pump can deliver at most 600 L/min total, so overlapping zones must add up to no more than that. My water allocation is 52,000 L per day. No zone may run longer than 90 minutes. Nothing runs between 11:00 and 16:00 because of power prices ($0.31/kWh peak versus $0.11 off-peak), and I'd rather not run anything within an hour after dusk, which is about 18:40 this month. Cherries are never watered the 3 days before picking, which starts Oct 28 for Bing. Also, the 4 apple zones should not all be watered on consecutive days.

Build me a page where I can change times, durations and days, with the rules checked as I go and clear explanations when something breaks, and give me an easy way to choose start times and weekly patterns. At the end let me copy out the schedule in the same layout as the export above so I can enter it into the controller.
